lms: Canvas (Instructure), systemwide; migrated from self-hosted Moodle (Canvas selected 2017, transition complete Summer 2019)
ai_guidance: The Provost's office provides central guidance ('AI and your classroom,' sample GenAI syllabus statements) leaving course-level AI rules to instructor discretion, complemented by the systemwide 'Navigating AI @ UMN' portal from OIT and Teaching Support/LATIS instructor guides. UMN explicitly does not endorse AI-detection tools and recommends against scanning student work with detectors.
enterprise_ai_tools: Google Gemini with enterprise-grade data protection for all students, faculty, and staff (data stays within UMN, not used to train models), Google NotebookLM, and Microsoft Copilot Chat with data protection via UMN sign-in; approved only for Public-classified data unless otherwise approved. No ChatGPT Edu agreement found.
notable: Launched a university-wide AI Hub in March 2026 under inaugural Vice Provost for AI Galin Jones, part of the Elevate Extraordinary 2030 roadmap. Notable controversy: PhD student Haishan Yang was expelled over alleged AI use on a 2024 exam and sued; the Minnesota Court of Appeals upheld the expulsion in February 2026.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion: the Provost publishes customizable sample GenAI syllabus statements ranging from 'no restrictions' to complete prohibition; unauthorized AI use is handled as scholastic dishonesty under the Student Conduct Code.
